question:
A group compares inverse tangent and inverse cotangent using $u=\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3})$ and $v=\cot^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$. The principal-value range of $\tan^{-1}x$ is $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, whereas the principal-value range of $\cot^{-1}x$ is $(0,\pi)$. Although $\tan u=-\sqrt{3}$ and $\cot v=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ describe the same tangent ratio, the inverse functions return angles from different intervals. The group uses the property $\tan^{-1}x+\cot^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ for every real $x$ to compare the two values and determine their relationship.

(a) Determine the principal value of $u$.

(b) Determine the principal value of $v$.

(c) Calculate $v-u$.

(d) Verify $\tan^{-1}x+\cot^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ for $x=-\sqrt{3}$.
explanation:
(a)
The angle in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ whose tangent is $-\sqrt{3}$ is $-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Therefore,
$$u=\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3})=-\frac{\pi}{3}$$

(b)
Since
$$\cot\frac{2\pi}{3}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$
and $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\in(0,\pi)$, the principal value is
$$v=\cot^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=\frac{2\pi}{3}$$

(c)
Using the values of $u$ and $v$,
$$v-u=\frac{2\pi}{3}-\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\pi$$
Hence, the two principal values differ by $\pi$.

(d)
For $x=-\sqrt{3}$,
$$\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3})=-\frac{\pi}{3}$$
Also,
$$\cot^{-1}(-\sqrt{3})=\frac{5\pi}{6}$$
Therefore,
$$\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3})+\cot^{-1}(-\sqrt{3})=-\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{5\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{2}$$
Thus, the property is verified.
